A contract signed by both parties, dated, identifying the vehicle by its chassis number, establishes ownership; when the certificate is in a third party’s name, request the full chain of deeds from the registered person to your seller to you. Without proof, SNCA registers you as holder, but the certificate notes the holder is not identified as owner.

blocks.q: Do I need to redo the technical inspection when arriving in Luxembourg?
blocks.a: Not if the foreign inspection is still valid. A certificate issued in another Member State or Switzerland remains valid but its duration becomes that of Luxembourg law: first inspection 4 years after first registration, second 2 years later, then annually.

blocks.q: What is the deadline to register a vehicle I bring with me?
blocks.a: Within six months of the arrival declaration at the municipality. Before going to SNCA, you need the registration number, Luxembourg insurance, and the Customs sticker 705, which is required even when no VAT is due.

blocks.q: How do you register an imported vehicle?
blocks.a: It depends on your case. Import: technical inspection, insurance, then registration. Buying from a professional: they handle it. Buying between private individuals: the process is yours, with both parts of the certificate.

title: Insuring Your Vehicle
summary: Mandatory before driving, and the information statement from your previous insurer is valuable.

sources.title: France, contenu du relevé d'information, annexe à l'article A121-1

blocks.text: Liability insurance is mandatory for every registered vehicle, and the certificate is required at the time of registration. It must therefore be taken out before, not after.
The information statement is a right, not a favor

The factor that most affects the premium is your claims history, and the document that reports this is called relevé d'information in France, attestation de sinistralité in Belgium, and certificat bonus-malus in Luxembourg. It is the same document. Since the 2021 European directive on motor insurance, your insurer must provide it within fifteen days of your request, and it covers at least the past five years. An insurer from another Member State must take it into account just as it would a national document: the directive prohibits treating a driver differently based on nationality or previous country of residence.
Request it before cancelling. After cancellation it is still due, but you often need to follow up.
If you have never had a contract in your name

This applies to those who drove a vehicle owned by a parent, spouse, or stepparent without being listed on the contract. The statement belongs to the policyholder and only names the drivers designated on the contract: your relative’s does not mention you, and their no-claims bonus does not transfer to you.

Practically, you start at the neutral level of the Luxembourg scale, which runs from -3 to 22, where level 11 corresponds to the base premium. This is not a barrier: no statement is required to insure or register a vehicle; it only affects the price. Two things are worth trying: ask your relative’s insurer for a written certificate confirming you drove the vehicle without claims, which a Luxembourg insurer may choose to accept or not, and have yourself added as a designated driver on a contract while you drive without having one in your own name.
What distinguishes insurance contracts

Beyond mandatory liability coverage, so-called all-risk policies also cover damage to your own vehicle. Useful comparisons focus on specific points: the amount of deductibles, whether roadside assistance is provided from home or only beyond a certain distance, availability of a replacement vehicle, and coverage for glass breakage.

As with home insurance, these elements appear in the general conditions and not the quotation. Request the standardized information document, general conditions, and special conditions: two contracts at the same price can differ significantly in terms of deductible and assistance, which are precisely what you will notice on the day of a claim.
Key points to remember

Insurance is mandatory before registration. The information statement must be requested within fifteen days; it is a right. Without a contract in your name, you are placed at the neutral level, and nothing is blocked. Compare deductibles and assistance, not just the premium.
Frequently Asked Questions

blocks.q: Is an information statement required to insure a car in Luxembourg?
blocks.a: It is not required, neither for insurance nor for registration: it only affects the price. If you have had a contract in your name, request it—it is your right: your insurer must provide it within fifteen days and it covers at least five years. Without a contract in your name, there is nothing to request, and you start at the neutral level of the Luxembourg scale, level 11 on a scale from -3 to 22.

blocks.q: I drove a relative’s car without being listed on the contract; does that count?
blocks.a: Not automatically. The statement belongs to the policyholder and only lists drivers designated on the contract: your relative’s does not mention you. You can ask their insurer for a written certificate confirming you drove without claims, but no Luxembourg insurer is obliged to accept it. Being listed as a designated driver avoids this issue going forward.

title: Free Public Transport
summary: Completely free since February 2020, but service varies greatly depending on the municipality.

blocks.text: Since February 29, 2020, public transport has been free for everyone throughout the entire territory: buses, trams, and second-class trains, without needing to purchase a ticket. Free access also applies to cross-border workers, but only on the Luxembourg portion of their journey. Only first-class train travel remains charged.

This free transport has a greater impact on a family budget than one might think, and can legitimately call into question the purchase of a second car. However, service must keep up: the network is dense around the capital and along railway lines, but significantly sparser in rural areas, where a car often remains essential.

Before choosing a municipality, therefore, check the actual schedules from the nearest stop, at the times that concern you, and not just the existence of a line. Free park-and-ride facilities on the outskirts also allow for combining car and train travel, and help avoid expensive and limited city parking.
Key Points
Free everywhere, without needing a ticket. Check the real service before choosing a municipality. Can call into question the purchase of a second car.
Frequently Asked Questions

blocks.q: Is public transport really free?
blocks.a: Yes, since February 2020, throughout the entire territory and for everyone, including cross-border workers on the Luxembourg portion of their journey. Only first-class train travel remains charged.

title: Internet and Telephony
summary: Highly variable delays depending on the season, a provisional solution to request, and free mediation.

blocks.text: The main fixed operators are POST, the historic operator, as well as Orange, Tango, Eltrona, and Luxembourg Online. Fiber covers the main localities, but eligibility must be checked at the exact address, not just the municipality: in old buildings, the connection may stop at the foot of the building.
Delays Depending on the Season

Expect two to three weeks between subscription and installation during normal periods. This average can be misleading: the months with high mobility, typically from June to September, the time for moves and new school years, considerably lengthen delays, sometimes beyond one month. The end of the year and holiday periods have the same effect for another reason: the number of available technicians decreases.

If your home is not yet connected, a two-visit intervention may be necessary, one to bring the fiber and another to install the equipment. Each visit requires your presence, and a missed appointment can be charged. Have the date and time slot confirmed in writing, and immediately report any access particularities, such as a street number or intercom name different from that on the contract.
Don’t Stay Without Connection
Always request a provisional 4G solution: several operators lend one during the waiting period, but rarely without it being asked for. This reflex prevents starting teleworking without a connection.
Choosing Your Offer

Offers often combine internet, fixed line, and television, with a commitment of twelve to twenty-four months. A simple rule should be remembered: upgrading is possible at any time, downgrading rarely. So start small, you can adjust later. Provide an ID, the lease or deed of ownership, and your bank details.
In Case of Dispute

The mediation service of the Institut luxembourgeois de régulation is competent for disputes with an operator, and its referral is free. One condition is mandatory: you must have sent a written complaint to the operator and received no response, or an unsatisfactory response. A phone call, even if followed by an explicit refusal, does not fulfill this condition. Write, and keep proof.
Key Points
Two to three weeks, but more from June to September. Request provisional 4G; it is not offered automatically. In case of dispute: written complaint first, then free mediation.
Frequently Asked Questions

blocks.q: How long does it take to get internet?
blocks.a: Two to three weeks during normal periods, but significantly longer from June to September, the moving season. Request a provisional 4G solution: several operators lend one, rarely without being asked.

title: Languages and Integration
summary: Three administrative languages, English widely used at work, and subsidized courses.

blocks.text: The country operates with three administrative languages. French dominates in administration and shops, German in the press and primary school, Luxembourgish in social and community life. English has become established in the financial and European sectors, to the point that it is possible to work there long-term without speaking the other three.

However, this flexibility has a clear limit: Luxembourgish becomes indispensable for naturalization, as well as for many public service jobs or positions involving contact with the public. If either is part of your plans, start early, as the required level takes time to achieve.

The Institut national des langues offers reduced-price courses in all four languages, with evening sessions adapted for employees. Municipalities and the adult education service also organize courses, often cheaper and closer to home, with the advantage of meeting other neighborhood residents.
Key Points
Three administrative languages, plus English at work. Luxembourgish is a condition for naturalization. Subsidized courses at the INL and in municipalities.
Frequently Asked Questions

blocks.q: Is Luxembourgish necessary for work?
blocks.a: It depends on the position. Three languages are administrative: French, German, and Luxembourgish, and English is widespread in international companies. However, public service jobs often require all three of the country's languages.

blocks.q: Should I learn Luxembourgish?
blocks.a: Not for work: English and French suffice in many sectors. However, yes for naturalization and many public service jobs. Subsidized courses are available.

title: Luxembourg Nationality
summary: Dual nationality is allowed, but naturalization requires long-term residence and a language test.

blocks.text: Luxembourg allows dual nationality: becoming Luxembourgish does not require renouncing your original nationality. This is a significant difference from several neighboring countries, and it explains the interest of many long-term residents in the procedure.

The main route is naturalization. It requires a minimum period of regular residence, passing a spoken Luxembourgish test, and attending civic instruction courses. Other routes exist depending on family circumstances, especially for children born in Luxembourg or people with a Luxembourgish ancestor.

The exact conditions, particularly the required length of residence and expected language level, have changed several times in recent years. Check them on the official information sheet before starting anything, and especially plan ahead for the language part, which is by far the longest to prepare.
Key Points
Dual nationality allowed. Spoken Luxembourgish test and civic instruction required. Check the required residence duration as it changes.
Frequently Asked Questions

blocks.q: How long does it take to obtain nationality?
blocks.a: Naturalization requires long-term residence and a language test. The language part is the longest to prepare, so it is worth starting courses in the first year if you are interested in naturalization, rather than waiting until it becomes mandatory.

blocks.q: Is it possible to have dual nationality?
blocks.a: Yes, Luxembourg allows it. Naturalization requires long-term residence, a spoken Luxembourgish test, and civic instruction courses. Plan ahead for the language part.

title: Waste and Community Life
summary: The municipality provides the bins, publishes the schedule, and grants access to the recycling center.

blocks.text: Waste management is entirely the responsibility of the municipality: it provides the bins, publishes the collection schedule, and grants access to the recycling center. Sorting is detailed, with separate collection days for household waste, paper and cardboard, glass, packaging, organic waste, and green waste.

Bulky items and special waste can be dropped off at the recycling center, often upon presentation of proof of residence. Locate its location and opening hours as soon as you move in: this is precisely when people produce the most cardboard and dispose of furniture.

More broadly, the municipality is the point of contact for many everyday services: certificates, residential parking permits, school and extracurricular registrations, chèque-service accueil (a service voucher). Obtaining the collection schedule and identifying your municipal contact are among the steps that prevent many frustrations during the first weeks.
Key Points
Everything goes through the municipality. Locate the recycling center as soon as you move in. Obtain the collection schedule.
Frequently Asked Questions

blocks.q: How does waste sorting work?
blocks.a: Everything goes through the municipality: it provides the bins, publishes the collection schedule, and grants access to the recycling center. Obtain this schedule as soon as you move in.
